instructions: StationGod reads and changes a running Stationeers world. Each tool is a verb; most take what (the kind of thing) and share option names: find (lists), inspect (one thing in detail), survey (an area or network), read (live values), write (set values), plan (work out, change nothing), check (rules), build, swap (existing pieces), remove, move, trade, show (draw for the player), undo, server. help {verb, what} gives one in full. Targets: id (one, a list, or a ref "r3" from an earlier reply), near + radius, box, room, network. 'this', 'that' or 'here' is the thing the crosshair is on: inspect {what: "looking_at"}. build, swap, remove, move, trade, undo and cheats only report until confirm: true, and so does any write given a ref or network; ask the user before a cheat. For many things, give id a list or a ref. Shaping on every verb: fields, omit, list_limits, output_file, repeat (a ref: that call again), whole: true (lifts the cut of a reply over 12 KB; pages stay pages). For work across many replies or many targets, run_script. A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true. If the user says stop or hold: server {what: 'stop'}.

id.description: Target: an id, a list of ids, or a ref ("r3": the ids that reply showed).

rows.description: Rows each list of the report shows (0 for none); everything is still counted and checked.

near.description: Centre: [x, y, z], "player", "looking_at" or a thing's id (its position); with radius.

box.description: Two corners [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]].

network.description: A network: its id, a piece or device on it, or {id, port}.

prefab.description: Prefab: a whole name, a hash, or parts with * ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*': each part, any order); or a list of them.

name.description: Part of the shown name or label, any case.

limit.x-script: The first n in order (entries); left out, every one.

include.description: Parts to add to the reply.

verbose.description: The long form of the reply.

gateway.description: "world" (default) or a gateway id: only devices on its data networks.

confirm.description: true does it; left out, the call only reports what it would do.

queue.description: Wait in line behind a running job (up to 8) instead of answering busy.

max_wait.description: Seconds to wait for a confirmed job to finish before answering; 0 answers with its job id at once.

materials.description: Holder(s) that pay materials and take source refunds, tried in order; ids or "player". Default the player.

refund_to.description: Where removed materials go: a word (inventory, source, storage, ground, none), a container id, or a list tried in turn.

acknowledge_gas_lost.description: The job id whose gas loss you accept (with the user's agreement); lifts the gas hold.

fields.description: Keys to keep in each entry (dotted paths go deeper).

list_limits.description: {list: count}: keep more of a list cut by default.

output_file.description: true or a file name: the whole reply to a file, answered by a pointer.

whole.description: No 4 KB cut; pages stay pages (limit, offset).

repeat.description: A ref ("r7"): run that call again, the options given here replacing its own; then what and the other options may be left out.

from_plan.description: A ref of a plan route or plan spot reply ("r9"; one spot: "r9.spots.2", default the first): build its build_arguments; options given here are added.

types.Color: {index: int | None, name: str | None, is_default: bool}
types.Thing: {reference_id: str, prefab_name: str | None, display_name: str | None}
types.Error: {code: str, message: str, data: Any | None, see: {tool: str | None, topic: str, subtopic: str | None} | None}

topics.errors: A refusal is {code, message, fix}: message says what went wrong, fix what to do next; a fix never names an allow value. Missing or wrong options are one invalid_argument listing every problem: {code, message, problems: [{path, problem}], valid: [this what's own options, the nearest 3 first]}. write logic with no target is missing_target, naming id and writes. Every message uses verb names. game_unavailable: the MCP server could not reach the game; a write may have run if the game took the call.
topics.paging: A list answers one page: limit entries from offset, with total and has_more. Next page: repeat: "r3" with offset. order: nearest (default) or id (pages stay put). Every reply ends with truncated. Report lists use rows, not limit: rows is how many entries each list of a report shows, never a page. whole: true lifts the 4 KB cut only; it never fetches more pages. Each what's own limit maximum is in its help.
topics.positions:
A point is [x, y, z] or {x, y, z} in world metres, +y up. Building tools snap it to the cell it falls in: 0.5 m small cells for pieces and small devices, 2 m large cells for frames, walls and large structures; the reply's resolved says where it landed. Where a what's at says so, it also takes:
- "looking_at": where the player's look ray hits within 10 m. {looking_at: true, right, up, forward} moves it in the player's frame. Example: at: "looking_at".
- {relative_to, frame, right, up, forward, anchor}: a point beside a thing. relative_to takes "player", "looking_at" or an id; frame player, world or target; anchor origin, top, bottom, left, right, front or back of its footprint. Example: at: {relative_to: "4820585", right: 2}.
- {on_face: true, along_right, along_up}: a point on the 2 m face plane you look at, right and up as you see them. Example: at: {on_face: true, along_right: 1}.
Every length is metres. no_crosshair_hit or no_face when the ray hits nothing; these need the player's view.
topics.refs:
Replies that are reports, plans, cut, or lists with has_more or 3 or more ids carry ref: "rN". The MCP server keeps the call and its whole reply until a world is loaded. A script run's id (script-14) is a ref to its returned value (sg.ref('script-14') in a script).
- As a target: id: "r3" is the ids that reply showed (see targets). A write whose target came from a ref reports first, with targets: {from, ids, more_in_source}.
- repeat: "r7" runs call r7 again, with the options you give replacing its own (what may be left out). repeat: "r7", confirm: true runs the report r7 for real on exactly the targets it listed. A plain repeat always calls the game; only a repeat that changes fields, omit or whole of a reply that is not a live value is answered from the store, marked from_store.
- from_plan: "r9" on build builds a plan route's or spot's build_arguments ("r9.spots.2": that spot).
topics.shaping:
The reply cap: a direct reply over 12 KB (some whats set their own threshold, named in their help) to a call that asked for no size is cut to about 4 KB; a report, whole: true, output_file, a paging limit above the default and list_limits are never cut. A cut reply keeps as much as fits, in this order: whole entries of its main list; else every entry in a shallow form (plain values kept, nested lists as their length, small objects kept, others as {...}); else the first shallow entries. With several lists, each is cut in proportion. It adds ref, cut ("8384 B; cells 4 of 8 shallow, pieces 9 of 18 shallow") and next: whole: repeat 'r4' with whole: true (~2620 tokens) | page: repeat 'r4' with offset: 8 | as a target, r4 is the shown entries.
fields [keys]: keep only these keys; a dotted path goes deeper. omit [paths]: leave keys out. list_limits {list: n}: keep more of a list cut by default. output_file: true or a file name: the whole reply to a file, answered by a pointer. Unknown fields names come back in fields_unmatched with fields_closest. Errors are never cut or shaped.
topics.targets:
Every verb names what it acts on the same way.
- id: one id, a list of ids, or a ref, where a what takes them (its help says; a what that takes one id says "One id"). A ref is the ids an earlier reply showed you: "r3" (its main list: the page, or the shown entries of a cut reply), "r3.members", "r4.rockets.parts" (a path through lists), "r9.spots.2" (one entry). For more than was shown, repeat the call with a larger limit. Any thing id may be "looking_at" (the thing the crosshair is on); "player" where a what says so. A rocket id may be its name ('Tanker').
- A list of ids where one is expected answers {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, ...} or {index, ok, reference_id, error}], count, success_count, error_count}; fields paths are results.<key>. A typed list past the handler's maximum is refused, naming it.
- near + radius: around [x, y, z], "player", "looking_at" or a thing's id (its position), radius in metres. Each what says what near left out means; radius without near, or near "player" without radius, is refused.
- box: two corners [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]]. room: a room id. network: a network id, a piece or device on it, or {id, port}.
- prefab: a whole name, a hash (an integer, or a string of digits), or parts with *, each part matched in any order ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*'); or a list, any of which matches. A name or pattern that matches nothing answers prefab_not_found with the 3 nearest.
- name: part of the shown name or label, any case (a * in it is ignored). Players are named with player and to_player.
Lengths are metres and times seconds; other units are in the option's name.
topics.writes:
build, swap, remove, move, trade buy and sell, undo, and every cheat only report until confirm: true. A write given ids you typed out acts at once; a write whose targets you did not type out (a ref, a network, a spread) reports until confirm: true, listing every target with its current value under targets. Every report, direct or scripted, carries report_only: true. A report is never cut; its problems, warnings, will_burst, gas_check, passed and targets stay whatever fields or omit say. A report too large for the client answers report_too_large with the target count and how to narrow it.
Bulk work is split by the MCP server into calls each handler takes (place 64, paint 256, label 64, logic 256, remove 256), sent one after another; a refused one stops the rest, named in not_run. A confirmed bulk write is undone as write-N.
Jobs (build, swap, remove, undo) run one at a time; queue (default true) waits in line. A confirmed job, or gas move, answers when it is done, up to max_wait seconds (default 30, at most your client's timeout), with held_ms (how long it paused the game); after that it answers its id: inspect {what: "job", id}. Nothing fills in a default for you.
Undo: undo {id} takes back a build or removal job; swap jobs cannot be undone. A bulk write's undo takes back the steps marked [undo] in its report, newest first, one step at a time; it stops at a refused step, and from_step goes on.
Cheats change the world as a player cannot: move gas and player, write memory, battery and genes, server command (read-only commands too), build blueprint, free: true, force: true. Ask the user before each.
allow: [names] lifts a named guard for this call: door_keepout, split, contents, breach, broken, burst, unsupported, in_use, ground, off_network, out_of_range, overwrite, pad, lint. A call that lifted a guard lists the codes it passed in passed. A build that pays from the player's inventory warns materials_from_player. A write or report on a device that a chip, logic writer, screen script or another run drives warns driven_by (inspect controllers). A write that turns on or opens a vent, valve or pump is refused on a network lint problem unless allow: ["lint"].
topics.scripts:
A run is one call. A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true. confirm inside the code is refused: invalid_argument: confirm belongs to the run.
- What counts as seen (one rule for direct calls and scripts): ids the MCP server showed you this session (direct reply entries, report rows, a run's printed or returned value within its cut); any int or str constant in the run's code, f-string pieces included (a target passes when its value equals one of them); selectors written in the code (a network, a spread, a ref such as sg.ref('r7')); what this run builds (placed, swap results); "player".
- Report runs. run_script {code} reports every write (report_only: True), act-at-once writes included, and acts on nothing. The reply lists every target as [id or cell, name, current -> new], with its undo mark and any lifted guard (a very large report is summarised; past the client's limit it answers report_too_large). Builds report placed: [], so writes on what the run would build are not shown. Waits are real until the run's first write. After a write, the second wait inside a while or watch loop ends the pass with a BaseException, so finally runs and its writes are reported; finite for loops run through. One header line gives the report's limits: reads after a reported write show the old value; a waiting loop runs once; writes on what this run builds are not shown. for loops over found things list every target.
- Confirmed runs. run_script {code, confirm: true} acts as it goes on seen targets. An unseen target (such as ids a find inside the run returned that you never saw) before anything acted: the run goes on as a report run, and the reply is the report: unseen targets at line 7: nothing acted; this is the report; confirm it with run_script {repeat: "script-17", confirm: true}. After something acted: the run stops with sg.Stopped(unseen_targets, line, targets) before that write. After a stop the hub refuses the run's writes except held restores and writes in the finally or __exit__ it unwinds through (footered CLEANUP). The stop reply lists the remaining targets as report rows, so they are now seen, and says repeat (only undoable writes acted) or undo script-N first. A stopped run is not resumed.
- Repeat. run_script {repeat: "script-14", confirm: true} runs script-14's code again on fresh reads, under the same seen rule; the report's rows are seen. Logic values may differ from the report: the footer's DIFFERS FROM REPORT group shows them, and undo covers them. [cannot undo] writes (chip source, console command, screen press, uplink, flight log, trades, store moves) must have the whole argument set equal to the report's for that target, or the run stops. repeat_expired: the report was made in another world, or its record was dropped.
- Waiting. sg.wait(s) waits s seconds and returns None; time.sleep is sg.wait. sg.watch(reads, until, timeout) -> (rows, met): reads is a list of read logic reads entries ({'id': tank, 'logic': 'Pressure'}); until(rows) gets the rows, one per entry, in order, and returns a bool; rows is the last read. The watch ends when until returns True (met True) or after timeout seconds (met False); it never raises at timeout. It follows subscriptions where they cover the values, and otherwise polls once a second (light reads) or every 5 s (heavy ones). Repeating work (until X, or for N minutes) is one run with a loop: sg.watch, or a loop with sg.wait.
- Restores. with sg.hold(id, logic, value=None, after=<value before>): writes value, and restores after on exit (normal, exception or stop); the mod also applies it at session end or after an unresumed disconnect, in the same world and while the target still holds the run's last written value. Logic writes only, on seen targets. Reports show 'on exit: pump On -> 0'. It is the taught restore: plain finally runs on stops and run ends, but not at session end.
- A run is a job. max_wait is how long this reply waits (default 30 s for confirmed runs; up to the client's limit, 600 s, for report and read-only runs), at most your client's timeout; the run goes on until its code ends, it is stopped, or the session ends. A reply before the end says what the run waits on: script-14 running: line 4, sg.watch timeout 480 s, 37 s in, +3 write logic. Follow it with inspect {what: "job", id: "script-14"} (its own max_wait). inspect {what: "job"} with no id lists runs with notices pending.
- Notices. Notices and cost lines name the run's id and its first code line, and end "if you did not start it, leave it". A done notice comes once, on run_script and inspect job replies. A run that left something (stopped or killed with changes not restored, or writes not done) is one sticky line on every reply until you inspect it or undo it by id.
- Stop. server {what: "stop", id: "script-14"} stops one run; server {what: "stop"} stops every live run and answers the ids and first lines it stopped. A user cancel and the end of the session stop runs too. The run gets sg.Stopped (a BaseException: except Exception does not catch it) once, at its next sg call (at once inside a wait or watch), so finally blocks run: reads and writes still act there, waits and watches raise at once. The worker is killed 5 s after the stop (longer while an sg call is in flight, never past 30 s), or on a second stop. The stop reply lists what the run changed and did not restore (left: 4612280 On=1, set line 3) and each job in flight. A world change stops every live run and refuses later writes, finally included; held restores are dropped.
- The session. A run ends with this session; it is not a safety interlock; anything that must keep running belongs in a chip. A journal keeps each run's end state: the next session's first reply says in one line when something was left.
- Undo. undo {id: "script-14"} reverts the whole run, newest first, restoring each target to its value before the run; groups that cannot be undone are named [cannot undo]. A target changed since the run's last write (by the user, a chip or another run) is reported and not written unless allow: ["overwrite"]. It reports first; confirm: true undoes. Undo of a running run is refused: stop it first. After a world change it answers undo_expired.
- Warnings. A write on a device that a chip, logic writer, screen script or another run drives carries driven_by (inspect {what: "controllers", id} lists them); a vent, valve or pump opened runs the network lint. In a run they are gathered in the WARNINGS footer and report group. A run that re-reads a value it wrote and finds it changed lists it under CONTESTED.
- Cost lines. A run alive past its first reply has one line: calls, writes by verb and what, and game ms since the last line, and how to stop it. It rides every run_script, inspect job and server info reply, and other replies at most once every 10 minutes.
- The returned value. The code runs as a function body; return x, or a final bare expression. Past 4 KB the rest is in the run's ref; sg.ref('script-12') gives it as stored (a JSON round trip); sg.ref('r7') gives a direct reply as a dict, whole.
- Calls. Script calls mint no refs and are never cut. Iterating a reply dict raises TypeError: iterate r['things'] (the main list). The main list is walked by cursor in a single for; len, an index, sorted or a second pass pages in the rest first. offset is refused; limit is the first n in order. A script call waits for its job.
- Errors raise sg.Error(code, message, fix, maybe_ran). A failed run's reply gives: line N and its source; the exception and message; for sg.Error the call sent, code, fix and maybe_ran; for a KeyError on a reply dict, the keys it has, nearest first; the values of the names on that line; then the footer. print of a list of row dicts prints a table.

What run replies look like:

returned: {'start_kpa': 2101.5, 'end_kpa': 8004.2, 'met': True}
DONE write logic x2 (4612280 On)
undo script-14 while this session lasts (logic writes)
cost script-14 (pump = '4612280'): 243 calls, 2 writes, 6.2 game ms over 241 frames, 0 frames over budget, held tick 0 ms, 251 s wall

script-15 REPORT: nothing changed; run_script {repeat: "script-15", confirm: true} does it
limits: reads after a reported write show the old value; a waiting loop runs once; writes on what this run builds are not shown
REPORTED write logic x3 [undo]:
  [4701001, Wall Light 1, On 1 -> 0]
  [4701002, Wall Light 2, On 1 -> 0]
  [4701007, Wall Light (hall), On 1 -> 0]

topics.types: Shared reply types. The small ones (Thing, Vec3, Error, Color, LogicType) are written out on the Types line of each stub that uses them. Job views come one per call: help {topic: "types", subtopic: "<name>"} or sg.help('types', '<name>'). Names: BuildJob, GasCheck, JobBusy, JobQueued, JobDropped, RefundPlan, RunJob, SwapJob, UpgradeJob, UndoJob.
